title: Geometric inverse image compares standard algebra resolutions and differential complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in a common universe of sheaf values and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], with inverse image $F=f^{-1}$. For a ring sheaf $R$ and a sheaf of sets $E$ on $\mathcal C$, write $R[E]$ for the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $U\mapsto R(U)[E(U)]$, the polynomial algebra whose variables are indexed by $E(U)$. There is a canonical isomorphism of $FR$-algebras $F(R[E])\cong(FR)[FE]$ carrying the inverse images of the coefficient and variable maps to the coefficient and variable maps. It commutes with the evaluation counit and free-algebra unit.
For a map $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ of commutative ring sheaves, let $P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $P_{n+1}=\mathcal A[P_n]$ with the evaluation faces, unit degeneracies and iterated evaluation augmentation. Let $P'_\bullet$ be this same augmented simplicial construction for $F\mathcal A\to F\mathcal B$. The preceding comparisons induce an isomorphism $FP_\bullet\cong P'_\bullet$ of augmented simplicial algebras, respecting every face and degeneracy. With sheaf differentials the sheafifications of the sectionwise modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], there are compatible isomorphisms of simplicial $F\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]
$$F(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}\mathcal B)\cong\Omega^1_{P'_\bullet/F\mathcal A}\otimes_{P'_\bullet}F\mathcal B.$$
They carry the inverse image of the universal differential and coefficient tensor maps to their corresponding maps for $P'_\bullet$. If $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$, with alternating-face differential and zero positive terms, they induce an actual complex isomorphism $F s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}\mathcal B)\cong s(\Omega^1_{P'_\bullet/F\mathcal A}\otimes_{P'_\bullet}F\mathcal B)$, and its isomorphism in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All these comparisons are natural in commutative squares of ring sheaves. For the identity geometric morphism they are identities; for composite geometric morphisms they agree with the successive comparisons under the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphisms. The statement includes presheaf topoi, represented by sites with the topology in which only maximal sieves cover.

source.place: Tags 08SR (definition-standard-resolution-sheaves-rings), 08SS (definition-cotangent-complex-morphism-sheaves-rings), and 08SV (lemma-pullback-cotangent-morphism-topoi), including the free/forgetful square in its proof.

proof.text: First establish the free sheaf-algebra universal property. For an $R$-algebra sheaf $H$, a sheaf map $v:E\to|H|$ extends on each object uniquely to $R(U)[E(U)]\to H(U)$ by polynomial evaluation. Uniqueness on variables makes these extensions commute with every restriction. The sheafification universal property then extends them uniquely to an $R$-algebra map $R[E]\to H$. Conversely restrict an algebra map to the variable map $i_E:E\to|R[E]|$. These operations are inverse and natural. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-Alg}}(R[E],H)=\operatorname{Hom}(E,|H|)$; the unit is $i_E$, and the counit at $H$ evaluates the variable $[h]$ at $h$. No assertion that sheafification is computed sectionwise is used.

Put $V=f_*$. Apply the lifted ring-object adjunction to $F\dashv V$. For an $FR$-algebra $H$, regard $VH$ as an $R$-algebra through $R\xrightarrow{\eta_R}VFR\to VH$. The lifted adjunction restricts to $\operatorname{Hom}_{FR\text{-Alg}}(FQ,H)=\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-Alg}}(Q,VH)$: the equation on structure maps on one side is adjoint to the equation on the other, by naturality of the adjunction. With $Q=R[E]$, step 1 and the underlying set adjunction give $\operatorname{Hom}_{FR\text{-Alg}}(F(R[E]),H)=\operatorname{Hom}(E,V|H|)=\operatorname{Hom}(FE,|H|)$. Restriction along $Fi_E$ is this bijection. Consequently $F(R[E])$ and $(FR)[FE]$ both freely represent the same generator sheaf. Extend the generator map of each to the other using these bijections; both composites fix the generators, hence are identities. Denote the resulting isomorphism by $\theta_{R,E}:F(R[E])\to(FR)[FE]$. It carries the coefficient map to the coefficient map because it is an $FR$-algebra map, and $\theta_{R,E}Fi_E=i_{FE}$.

source.place: Tag 08SV, lemma-pullback-cotangent-morphism-topoi, free/forgetful square; lifted adjunction as in Sites Tag 00YV

proof.text: All free-algebra compatibility equations follow by the uniqueness in steps 1--2. For $r:R\to S$ and $v:E\to E'$, the two maps from $F(R[E])$ to $(FS)[FE']$ induced by $(r,v)$ have coefficient map $Fr$ and generator map $i_{FE'}Fv$, so they agree (view the target as an $FR$-algebra). For an $R$-algebra $Q$, the maps $F(R[|Q|])\to FQ$ given by $F\epsilon_Q$ and evaluation after $\theta_{R,|Q|}$ both send the generator $F|Q|$ identically to $F|Q|$, so they agree. The unit equation is exactly $\theta_{R,E}Fi_E=i_{FE}$. For $F=1$ this normalization forces $\theta=1$. For another geometric inverse image $G$, the two comparisons $GF(R[E])\to(GFR)[GFE]$ both carry the twice-transported coefficients and variable map to the prescribed ones. The representing property of step 2, applied also to $GF$, makes them equal. This proves composition coherence without assuming that transported local sections exhaust all sections.

source.place: Tag 08SV, compatibility of the free/forgetful square; Tag 08SR, evaluation and generator maps

proof.text: Write $T(Q)=\mathcal A[|Q|]$ and $T'(Q')=F\mathcal A[|Q'|]$. Step 1 is a free/forgetful adjunction, so the standard-adjunction resolution theorem supplies its augmented simplicial object with faces $T^i\epsilon T^{n-i}$ and degeneracies $T^i\delta T^{n-i}$, where $\delta$ is free applied to the unit. Start with $\alpha_{-1}=1_{F\mathcal B}$ and define recursively $\alpha_n=T'(\alpha_{n-1})\theta_{\mathcal A,|P_{n-1}|}$ for $n\geq0$, taking $P_{-1}=\mathcal B$. Each is an isomorphism. Step 3 intertwines both $\epsilon$ and $\delta$; inserting either in any one of the iterated factors and applying the recursion proves $\alpha_{n-1}F(d_i)=d'_i\alpha_n$ and $\alpha_{n+1}F(s_i)=s'_i\alpha_n$. The same counit equation proves augmentation compatibility. The operators reconstruction lemma now gives an augmented simplicial isomorphism. For a ring square $(a,b):(\mathcal A\to\mathcal B)\to(\mathcal A_1\to\mathcal B_1)$ the map in degree $-1$ is $b$, and in degree $n$ it is the polynomial map on coefficients $a$ and the previous degree's variables. Step 3 and induction prove naturality of $\alpha_n$. The identical recursion proves its identity and composition coherence.

source.place: Tags 08SR, 08SV; Simplicial Tag 08NC (lemma-standard-simplicial), operator formulas preceding that lemma

proof.text: For each $n$, first use the differential comparison to identify $F\Omega^1_{P_n/\mathcal A}$ with $\Omega^1_{FP_n/F\mathcal A}$, preserving the universal derivation. Transport along the algebra isomorphism $\alpha_n$ to get $\Omega^1_{P'_n/F\mathcal A}$. Apply the inverse-image tensor comparison over the ring sheaf $P_n$ to $\Omega^1_{P_n/\mathcal A}$ and $\mathcal B$ (the latter is a $P_n$-module by the augmentation). The finite-product lift is an algebraic inverse-image presentation; its exactness/existence is supplied by the geometric inverse-image lemma. After transporting the scalar ring $FP_n$ by $\alpha_n$, augmentation compatibility identifies the second tensor factor and its action with $F\mathcal B$. This constructs the required degreewise $F\mathcal B$-linear isomorphism $\beta_n$. In terms of universal maps its normalization is $F(\mathrm dp\otimes b)\mapsto\mathrm d(\alpha_n(Fp))\otimes Fb$, an equation of transported derivation and bilinear-pairing maps, not a sectionwise formula for $F$. In particular the coefficient tensor map $\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes1$ is preserved.

source.place: Tags 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials) and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), applied degreewise to Tag 08SS

proof.text: Check compatibility of $\beta_n$ using universal maps. The sheafified differential presentation says that module maps out of $\Omega$ are determined by the universal derivation; the tensor universal property says that maps out of $\Omega\otimes\mathcal B$ are determined by the associated bilinear map. For any face, degeneracy, or ring-square map $h:P_n\to Q_m$ with coefficient map $b:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B_1$, the differential-tensor map sends $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(hp)\otimes b(c)$. This follows by differentiating $h$ and then using the balanced tensor pairing. Applying the normalization of step 5 on either side gives $\mathrm d(\alpha^Q_m F(hp))\otimes F(bc)$, since step 4 gives $\alpha^Q_m Fh=h'\alpha^P_n$. The equations hold on universal derivation/pairing morphisms, so the two uniqueness properties imply equality of the module maps, including when the base ring changes. Thus the $\beta_n$ are a simplicial isomorphism and natural in all the stated ring squares. For an identity inverse image the normalized pairing is unchanged. For $GF$, both the direct comparison and the successive comparisons have the same universal derivation and pure-pairing images by step 3 and the coherence of the differential comparison. The same uniqueness gives their equality. This proves tensor and simplicial coherence, rather than inferring it from a bare degreewise isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 08TP, 08TQ, 03EL, and lemma-functoriality-differentials; Cotangent Tag 08SV, functorial free/forgetful square

proof.text: Let $M_\bullet=\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}\mathcal B$. The transported module inverse image preserves addition and zero: these operations are transported by finite products; in particular it is additive on module morphisms. It takes the zero module to zero (its underlying terminal sheaf stays terminal). Consequently $F(\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i d_i)=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i Fd_i$. Summing the face equations from step 6 gives $\beta_{n-1}F(d^{-n})=d'^{-n}\beta_n$ for every $n\geq1$; the degree-zero differential and positive terms are zero. The inverse family obeys the same equations by multiplying by the inverse isomorphisms, so this is an actual complex isomorphism. Apply the derived-category localization functor to it to obtain the claimed derived isomorphism. Naturality and identity/composition equations persist under taking the alternating complex and under this functor. Every construction above uses only a geometric morphism of the given small topoi, so it applies also to the maximal-sieve topology; no points, flatness or topological-space presentation was used.

The statement is the imported one. The three added stmt_deps (polynomial ring, sheaf tensor, algebraic inverse image) are notions it already uses. There are no new nodes, no cycle and no repair note. Step 1 is elementary: the polynomial universal property plus the sheafification universal property in rings. Step 2: F preserves finite products, so the lifted ring adjunction (2) applies. The R-algebra restriction is correct by naturality of the unit, and the composite bijection is restriction along Fi_E, so Yoneda gives θ. Step 3: naturality, the counit equation (|FQ|=F|Q|) and composite coherence (GF is a geometric inverse image; a^{-1}b^{-1} is literal) all follow by uniqueness. Step 4: the recursion α_n = T'(α_{n-1})θ is checked for d_0 via naturality of ε', for d_i = T(d_{i-1}) by induction, for degeneracies via θFi=i, and for the augmentation. The hypotheses of the operator-reconstruction and standard-resolution lemmas are met. Step 5: the hypotheses of lem-trf-topos-inverse-image-differentials and lem-pur-independent-inverse-image-tensor-comparison match the item's. ℬ is a P_n-module via the augmentation, and α intertwines it. Step 6: uniqueness from the derivation-representing and bilinear universal properties. Taking the universal generalized section (test sheaf |P|, p=id) avoids any assumption that sections are exhausted. Step 7: additivity is the graph condition of the algebraic inverse image. The face equations sum to the s(−) chain isomorphism, and Q gives the derived isomorphism. Edge cases checked: E=∅, the zero ring, F=id, the presheaf/chaotic topology, and degrees −1 and 0. No duplicates: the sfb flat-functorial/augmentation nodes are over topological spaces and cite the parent; simplicial-differential-base-change is ring base change only; sfb-internal-module-inverse-image-comparison is in the internal-module setting. I accept the three tool_uses as generic statements: the lifted ring adjunction, the normalized tensor comparison and the sheaf tensor bilinear universal property. No SGA is used.
